OUTSIDE RHEUMATOLOGY — FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 06/09/2025

Dear Colleague,

Ankylosing spondylitis follow-up. Mr. Burgos remains on adalimumab 40 mg every two weeks and sulfasalazine 1,000 mg twice daily, taking both as prescribed. Low back pain persists and is still worse on waking. No eye redness or pain since we last saw him. No diarrhea or abdominal pain. No infections.

Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: tenderness over the sacroiliac joints; lumbar flexion reduced, similar to prior.

Monitoring labs from your office reviewed — stable.

Plan: continue current therapy and home exercise program. Labs every three months. Return in six months or sooner as needed.

Rheumatology

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE RHEUMATOLOGY — FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 01/27/2026

Dear Colleague,

Mr. Burgos is a 29-year-old man with ankylosing spondylitis, diagnosed in January 2024, and beta thalassemia minor, seen for continuing care. He describes chronic, dull, deep pain across the lower spine and both hips that has gradually worsened over the past two years. It is worse in the morning or after he has been still for a while and better with activity. More recently, morning stiffness has been lasting about an hour before it eases. No trauma or unusual strain. When asked, he described a few episodes of eye redness and discomfort in recent months that cleared without treatment. No fevers, chills or weight loss.

Medications: adalimumab 40 mg subcutaneously every two weeks; sulfasalazine 1,000 mg twice daily.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family history: father with ankylosing spondylitis, who had back surgery in his forties.
Social: software engineer; describes himself as mostly sedentary now.

Examination: Gait normal. Lumbar flexion decreased and Schober's test positive. Chest expansion reduced. Tender over the sacroiliac joints.

Laboratory: inflammatory markers elevated. Rheumatoid factor negative. ANA negative.

Imaging: radiographs of the lumbar spine and sacroiliac joints today show changes suggestive of sclerosis and fusion of the sacroiliac joints.

Impression: ankylosing spondylitis with progressive symptoms on adalimumab and sulfasalazine; intermittent eye symptoms.

Plan: continue adalimumab and sulfasalazine at current doses. Daily stretching and mobility work. Your office to continue CBC and CMP every three months. Return in six months.

Rheumatology

documents.title: Rheumatology letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed rheum letter from 1/27: worsening inflammatory back pain and longer morning stiffness on adalimumab + sulfasalazine, reduced chest expansion, positive Schober, markers still up, RF/ANA negative. Films now suggest SI sclerosis/fusion. They're continuing the same regimen. A few recent episodes of eye redness that cleared on their own. Problem list current. Q3-month labs continue here.

documents.title: X-ray question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi — I saw the rheumatology letter in my portal. It says my x-rays show "sclerosis and fusion" of the SI joints. That sounds bad. What does that actually mean for me?

documents.title: RE: X-ray question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Fair question. Sclerosis means the bone around those joints has thickened, and fusion means the two sides of the joint have started to knit together — it's the way AS changes the sacroiliac joints over time. Those joints barely move to begin with, so it doesn't usually change what you can do day to day, and it's a separate question from the pain and stiffness, which is what treatment is aimed at. Your rheumatologist is keeping you on the same medicines for now. Happy to talk through it by phone or at a visit if you'd like.

ANNUAL PHYSICAL — 29M

AS: rheumatology letter from January reviewed — progressive symptoms, SI joints now showing sclerosis/fusion on film, same regimen continued. Today he says mornings are still the worst part, stiff for a good while after waking. Desk job; admits he's mostly sedentary these days. A couple of red, uncomfortable eyes over the winter that cleared on their own; none since.
Meds: adalimumab 40 mg SC q2wk, sulfasalazine 1,000 mg BID. NKDA.
Never smoker, no alcohol.

ROS: no fever, chills, weight loss, cough, GI symptoms.

Exam: vitals on flowsheet; weight up a couple of kilos from prior years. Well, NAD. Eyes quiet, no injection. Neck supple. RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. Spine: reduced lumbar flexion, tender SI joints. Gait normal. Skin clear.
PHQ-2: 0.

A/P:
1. AS — managed by rheumatology; their follow-up due this summer. CBC/CMP drawn today.
2. Recurrent anterior uveitis — quiet today. Same-day eye visit if redness with pain or light sensitivity.
3. Beta thalassemia minor — baseline.
4. Weight — encouraged regular movement; walking and the stretching rheum gave him.
5. HM: flu and COVID this fall. Tdap 2029.
